claims.statement: Cagrilintide is a long-acting amylin analog that mimics the endogenous hormone amylin; independent structural pharmacology shows it acts as a dual amylin and calcitonin receptor agonist, binding amylin receptors (AMY1R/AMY2R/AMY3R) in an amylin-like mode and also engaging the calcitonin receptor (CTR), inducing distinct conformational dynamics there that may contribute to its clinical efficacy, to influence appetite/satiety signaling and food intake. It is studied both as a monotherapy and, more prominently, coadministered with semaglutide (a GLP-1 receptor agonist) as the combination CagriSema.

remediation pass (2026-08-29): independently cross-checked against two Wikipedia tertiary sources citing the same NEJM DOI (10.1056/NEJMoa2502081). The Cagrilintide article reproduces the packet's exact figures (11.8% vs 2.3%; 31.6% vs 4.7%), but the separate CagriSema article states the cagrilintide-monotherapy arm as 11.5% (not 11.8%) — flagged as an unreconciled numeric discrepancy in the prior pass.

independent review (2026-08-29) RESOLVED this discrepancy: an independent trade-press clinical summary (Patient Care Online / HCPLive, materially different outlet than Pharmacy Times) confirms both figures are correct and reflect different statistical estimands — 11.8% is the primary trial-product estimand (the packet's cited figure), while 11.5% is a treatment-policy estimand that disregards adherence variation over the 68-week trial. This is not a real conflict between the two Wikipedia articles, just two valid analyses of the same trial. Separately, an independent systematic review/network meta-analysis (Hamarsheh et al. 2026, PMID 42207966, Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, 25 RCTs) ranks cagrilintide monotherapy behind CagriSema and tirzepatide/semaglutide in overall efficacy, consistent with this packet's framing. Full primary NEJM text access remains blocked (403/reCAPTCHA per the prior pass's attempts, not re-attempted this pass since independent secondary/tertiary corroboration resolved the specific discrepancy) and is an acceptable residual gap. Verdict: confirmed-with-note

claims.statement: Gray-market vendor and content pages marketing research-grade cagrilintide describe benefits in broader, more definitive terms than the controlled trial record supports — including claims of 'near-complete appetite loss' in some users, weight loss framed as being 'predominantly from fat mass, with preserved lean mass,' and self-administration titration schedules (e.g., weekly dose escalation from 0.16 mg to a 2.4 mg maintenance dose) presented as established protocol — despite cagrilintide having no FDA-approved product, no approved dosing regimen, and only trial-controlled (not self-administered, unsupervised) human safety data. A REDEFINE-1 body-composition sub-study for the CagriSema combination (not cagrilintide monotherapy) was presented at ECO 2026 (reported May 13, 2026): 66.9% of weight lost was fat mass and 33.1% was lean soft tissue overall, with the lean-tissue share of remaining body mass improving only at higher (≥30%) weight-loss thresholds. This is combination-product, not monotherapy, data, and it shows a still-substantial (~one-third) lean-tissue loss rather than 'preserved' lean mass as vendor pages frame it — so the available controlled body-composition evidence undercuts, rather than supports, the vendor marketing claim.

CORRECTED (2026-08-29, needs-adjustment finding): the prior claim that 'no controlled human body-composition data were located' was factually outdated. Independent review fetched a trade-press report (Pharmaceutical Technology) of a REDEFINE-1 CagriSema body-composition sub-study presented at ECO 2026 (May 13, 2026, before this packet's original 2026-08-28 generation date). This data (a) is for the CagriSema combination, not cagrilintide monotherapy, so it does not directly validate vendor claims about standalone cagrilintide; and (b) shows real, non-trivial lean-tissue loss (~33% of total weight lost), which undercuts rather than supports the vendor's 'preserved lean mass' framing. Net effect: the misinformation-adjacent conclusion (vendor claims overstate/mischaracterize the evidence) still holds and is arguably strengthened, but the factual premise ('no data exists') has been corrected.

conflicts.summary: Vendor/content marketing pages describe body-composition-specific (fat-vs-lean mass) and extreme appetite-suppression outcomes for cagrilintide that were previously believed unsupported by any located trial evidence. RESOLVED (2026-08-29): a REDEFINE-1 CagriSema body-composition sub-study (ECO 2026, reported May 13, 2026) was independently located, showing 66.9% of weight lost was fat mass and 33.1% lean soft tissue. This data is CagriSema-specific (not cagrilintide monotherapy) and shows a still-substantial lean-tissue loss that contradicts, rather than supports, the vendor pages' 'preserved lean mass' framing — the specific factual gap (whether body-composition data exists) is now closed, and the underlying misinformation-adjacent concern about vendor overclaiming is corroborated, not resolved away.
